hero.title: Explainable multimodal emotion analysis from children's drawings
hero.subtitle: This prototype classifies children's drawings into four emotion categories using a ResNet-50 + Clinical Feature fusion architecture trained on the hand-labeled KIDO dataset, and delivers explainable decision-support outputs to assist expert review.
highlights: 4-class emotion classifier (Happy / Sad / Angry / Fear) trained on 6,619 drawings (KIDO, hand-labeled)
ResNet-50 + 18 clinical feature fusion — Test Macro F1: 0.833 / Accuracy: 83.2%
Temperature Scaling calibration (T*=2.65), Grad-CAM visualization, and LLM clinical report generation

home.panelTitle: The report distilled into one screen
home.panelSubtitle: The system processes the drawing image alongside 18 OpenCV-derived clinical features to produce an emotion classification, complemented by Temperature Scaling calibration, Grad-CAM visual explainability, and an LLM-generated clinical report.
panelFlow: The drawing is accepted as input, resized to 224×224, and normalized with ImageNet statistics.
18 clinical features are extracted with OpenCV (line density, color distribution, sharp-angle ratio, etc.).
ResNet-50 visual branch and Clinical MLP outputs are fused and classified into 4 emotion classes; calibrated with T*=2.65.
home.quickCardOneText: ResNet-50 visual backbone (2048-dim output) and an 18-feature Clinical MLP are fused in a joint head, yielding a 25M-parameter classifier.
home.quickCardTwoText: Grad-CAM heatmaps + LLM-generated clinical report. Low-confidence cases are flagged as 'Uncertain' rather than forced into a class.

home.workflowTitle: From drawing to explainable clinical report
home.workflowIntro: The system is designed not just as a classifier but as a decision-support tool that provides the clinician with visual evidence and an interpretable report.

workflowSteps.title: Data preparation
workflowSteps.body: 5,177 drawings from the KIDO dataset were hand-labeled into four emotion classes. Minority classes were balanced to 1,100 via augmentation; the test set was held out entirely.

workflowSteps.title: Multimodal inference
workflowSteps.body: ResNet-50 visual features and 18 OpenCV-derived clinical features are fused in a shared head. Temperature Scaling (T*=2.65) reduces ECE from 0.1324 to 0.0231.

workflowSteps.title: Explanation and delivery
workflowSteps.body: Grad-CAM heatmap, rule-based and LLM-assisted clinical report, per-class confidence scores, and an 'Uncertain' flag below the confidence threshold are presented together.

home.modulesTitle: Model, calibration, explainability, and interface designed together
home.modulesIntro: The project goes beyond a training run: it delivers a calibration layer, an explainability stack, and a clinical-ready interface alongside the trained model.

modules.title: Data and experiment layer
modules.body: The KIDO dataset was hand-labeled; 7 architecture configurations were trained and compared (A1–A4: EfficientNet variants, B3–B5: ResNet-50, ResNet-18, ViT-B/16).

modules.title: Multimodal classification core
modules.body: ResNet-50 (visual branch, 2048→256) and Clinical MLP (18→128→64) are concatenated and classified via a 320→128→4 fusion head.

modules.title: Calibration module
modules.body: Post-hoc Temperature Scaling (T*=2.65) aligns model confidence with actual accuracy; ECE dropped from 0.1324 to 0.0231.

modules.title: Explainability and service
modules.body: Grad-CAM heatmaps, LLM clinical report generation, and a FastAPI + PyWebView desktop application turn the research output into a clinical prototype.

home.outcomesTitle: More than a model — an integrated clinical decision-support system
home.outcomesIntro: The project delivers a verifiable experiment infrastructure, calibration, explainability, and clinical presentation chain alongside the trained model.
outcomes: Reproducible training, evaluation, and calibration scripts for all 7 experiment configurations
Grad-CAM visualization + LLM-based clinical report generation with interpretable outputs
Temperature Scaling calibration and confidence-threshold-based 'Uncertain' decision mechanism
FastAPI REST API service and PyWebView desktop application
home.ethicsText: This system is not a clinical diagnosis tool. It is an explainable decision-support prototype designed to assist expert judgment; all outputs must be interpreted by a qualified psychologist or clinician.

about.objectiveText: This thesis developed an explainable multimodal deep learning system for automatic emotion classification from children's hand-drawn pictures. Based on the fusion of a ResNet-50 visual backbone with 18 OpenCV-derived clinical features, the system integrates Temperature Scaling calibration, Grad-CAM visual explainability, and LLM-based clinical report generation.

facts.label: Project title
facts.value: Emotion State Analysis with Deep Learning Methods from Children's Drawings

facts.label: Institution
facts.value: Nigde Omer Halisdemir University, Computer Engineering

goals: Hand-label the KIDO dataset into four emotion categories to build a reliable training source
Develop a multimodal classifier combining ResNet-50 backbone with 18 clinical features in a fusion architecture
Align model confidence scores with actual accuracy via Temperature Scaling calibration
Produce transparent decision-support outputs for clinicians via Grad-CAM and LLM-assisted explanations
about.dataIntro: The KIDO (Kinetic Family Drawing) dataset was used as the primary source. All labels were assigned manually by a single researcher; no pseudo-labels or model-guided labels were used.
dataPoints: Original total: 5,177 drawings — Happy: 2,963 · Sad: 1,456 · Angry: 359 · Fear: 399.
Minority classes (Angry, Fear) raised to 1,100 via augmentation; test set was excluded from augmentation.
Augmented total: ~6,619 samples. Test set: 993 samples (Happy: 445, Sad: 218, Angry: 165, Fear: 165).
Emotion classes: Happy, Sad, Angry, Fear — a 4-class classification task.
Training augmentation: ±15° rotation, horizontal flip, color jitter; val/test: resize + normalize only.
about.methodologyIntro: The system is built on the FlexibleFusionClassifier architecture, which combines a visual branch and a clinical feature branch. Seven configurations were evaluated comparatively.

methodologyCards.title: Overall architecture (B3 — best)
items: ResNet-50 backbone (ImageNet pretrained, 2048-dim output) → Linear(2048, 256) + ReLU + Dropout(0.2).
Clinical MLP: 18 features → Linear(18, 128) → ReLU → Linear(128, 64) — invalid features are zeroed.
Fusion: visual (256) + clinical (64) concatenated → Linear(320, 128) + ReLU + Dropout(0.3) → Linear(128, 4).

methodologyCards.title: Pre-processing
items: Images resized to 224×224 and normalized with ImageNet statistics.
Training augmentation: random rotation ±15°, horizontal flip, color jitter (brightness/contrast/saturation).
WeightedRandomSampler used to balance class frequencies during training.
18 clinical features: foreground area ratio, stroke darkness, sharp-angle ratio, warm-color ratio, etc.

methodologyCards.title: Training setup
items: Batch size: 32; early stopping patience: 7 epochs; best checkpoint by validation macro F1.
Weighted cross-entropy loss (class weights inversely proportional to frequency); seed=42.
7 configs: A1 (EffNet-B0), A2 (EffNet-B0+Clin), A3 (EffNet-B3), A4 (EffNet-B3+Clin), B3 (ResNet-50+Clin ★), B4 (ResNet-18+Clin), B5 (ViT-B/16+Clin).

methodologyCards.title: Calibration and explainability
items: Temperature Scaling: scipy NLL minimization on val-set logits; T*=2.65 found.
ECE before calibration: 0.1324 → after: 0.0231 (Brier score improvement: 0.282→0.131).
Grad-CAM: class-specific heatmap from last convolutional layer gradients.
LLM report: GPT-4o-mini via GitHub Models API; rule-based fallback if GITHUB_TOKEN is absent.

about.resultsIntro: 7 model configurations were compared. ResNet-50 + Clinical (B3) achieved the best performance across all metrics.
about.emotionResultsText: Per-class results on the 993-sample test set. Angry and Fear classes achieved the highest F1 scores.
about.genderResultsText: Individual class F1 scores on the test set. Sad scored lowest due to visual overlap with Happy.
deliverables: Reproducible training scripts and comparative evaluation infrastructure for all 7 experiment configurations
Temperature Scaling calibration module and confidence-threshold-based 'Uncertain' decision mechanism
Grad-CAM heatmaps, rule-based and LLM-assisted clinical explanation report generation
FastAPI REST API service + PyWebView desktop application as a clinical-ready prototype
limitations: Labeling was performed by a single researcher; inter-rater reliability (Cohen's κ) was not measured.
Sad class F1 (0.634) lags behind other classes due to visual overlap with Happy drawings.
The system has not yet been evaluated by psychologists in a real clinical setting.
LLM-based explanation requires external API access; privacy assessment may be needed in clinical environments.
futureWork: Re-labeling with larger and cross-cultural datasets and Cohen's κ measurement
Targeted augmentation and decision-boundary refinement for the Sad class
Deep learning-based clinical feature extraction (segmentation models)
Multi-task learning architectures that account for the child's developmental context
Systematic user study (psychologists and parents) for clinical utility and safety evaluation
Offline small language models (SLM) for privacy-preserving explanation generation
about.disclaimer: This system is not a clinical diagnosis tool; it should be used to support expert evaluation. All outputs must be interpreted by a qualified psychologist or clinician.
